space-grotesk.note: The body face wherever a room does not insist on its own, which puts it on the shared base EVERY page on the street loads. It ships as a variable font, so Google serves the same file for 400, 500 and 700 — it is downloaded ONCE here and declared three times against the weight axis, the same call Nunito, Cabin and Karla forced rather than storing identical bytes under three names. It WAS stored three times, byte for byte, until tools/pull-foundry.py hashed the shelf and said so; on the shared base that cost about 45KB. Identical bytes are not an absent bold — rendered out of this one file, 700 lays down 41% more ink than 400.
Byte-identical to the 400 above; see that note.

bitter.note: Bitter ships as a variable font, so Google serves the same file for every weight — 700 was byte-identical to this. The campgrounds takes the regular only and sets its emphasis in Alfa Slab One instead, rather than shipping 34KB twice under two names.

press-start-2p.note: The Arcade's only face, and the eighteenth family here. A pixel face is the one thing no other room can borrow without turning into the arcade — which is what 4.7KB buys. Latin subset only; the room sets nothing outside it.

bree-serif.note: The Latibulum's display face. A soft slab with round terminals — a beam somebody planed by hand rather than a letterpress serif, which is what keeps the burrow from reading like the Faery Yurt's high-contrast italic. Latin subset only.

nunito.note: The Latibulum's body face, and the only rounded sans on the street. It ships as a variable font, so Google serves the same file for 400 and for 700 — it is downloaded ONCE here and declared twice against the weight axis, the same call Bitter forced in the campgrounds rather than storing identical bytes under two names.

yeseva-one.note: The Jungle Room's display face. Its strokes THICKEN as they curve, which is the closest type gets to something grown rather than built — and it is what keeps a dark green room from sounding like the campground's routed park sign, which is incised and even-stroke. Latin subset only.

cabin.note: The Jungle Room's body face, and the caption under every leaf in it. A humanist sans, which is the plate-and-caption half of the pairing above. It ships as a variable font, so Google serves the same file for 400 and for 700 — downloaded ONCE and declared twice against the weight axis, the same call Nunito and Bitter forced.
Byte-identical to the 400 above; see that note.

ultra.note: The Den's display face. A fat 1970s slab — the weight a record sleeve was set in the year those sessions happened, and the one thing that keeps a green room off the Jungle Room upstairs, which sets a high-contrast serif that swells as it curves. Latin subset only.

karla.note: The Den's body face, and the sleeve notes on the back of that record. A grotesque with enough quirk to sit under a slab that heavy without disappearing. Variable, so one file serves 400 and 700 — stored once, declared twice against the weight axis, as Nunito, Bitter and Cabin already are.
Byte-identical to the 400 above; see that note.

im-fell-english.note: The Mopery (§22), and the face the Raven nook opens in. Igino Marini's digitisation of the types John Fell gave Oxford in the 1670s, ink spread and all — the one face here that looks IMPRESSED rather than drawn. Nothing else on this street is irregular like it: Cormorant Garamond is high-contrast and clean, Crimson Pro is a modern book serif.

spectral.note: The Mopery's reading face. A LOW-contrast screen serif, which is precisely what the Faery Yurt's Cormorant is not — the two warm-serif rooms stay apart at the stroke rather than at the palette. Not variable on Google, so 600 is a second file.

cinzel.note: The Oracle Deck (§23). Inscriptional Roman capitals — letters cut into stone rather than written — and nothing else on this street is cut. Ships as a variable font, so Google serves ONE file for 400 and 700: stored once and declared twice against the weight axis, the same as Nunito, Cabin and Karla.

cardo.note: The Oracle Deck's reading face. David Perry's classicist's type, drawn for people setting Greek and Old English beside Latin — a commentary face, which is what the back of every card in that deck is.

unifraktur-maguntia.note: The Doomscroll (§24), and DISPLAY ONLY — a masthead and the odd single word, never a line of the poems. Blackletter belongs on a doom broadside and not in the library two doors up, which is how the deliberately gothic room keeps the dark academia one from being cliche. Setting a poem in it would be an access failure dressed as atmosphere.

vollkorn.note: The Doomscroll's reading face, and the whole poem is set in it. Friedrich Althausen drew Vollkorn for body text at small sizes on bad paper, which is what a broadside is. Variable, so one file serves 400 and 600.

eb-garamond.note: Variable: the 400 file serves this weight against the wght axis, as Faustina's does.

bowlby-one-sc.note: The Outskirts (§34). The area's only face: fat, rounded small capitals, which is what a sign painted on a board by hand and left in the weeds looks like when headlights find it. Everything else out there is the shared base.

creepster.note: Black Leather Lagoon (§35), and the TITLE ONLY. A dripping monster-poster face is unreadable at length, so it sets the h1 and the bill and nothing else -- the Doomscroll's rule about blackletter, in the room most likely to talk itself out of it.

chivo.note: Black Leather Lagoon (§35), and everything in it that is not the title. A normal-width grotesque ON PURPOSE: the obvious choice for a poster's small print is a condensed gothic, and Club Chronic already sets Anton three doors up. The one room this must not collapse into is the one whose face the obvious choice would have borrowed. One variable file serves both weights, as Space Grotesk, Cinzel and Work Sans already do here.

italiana.note: Sithen (§36), and the h1 and headings only. A very thin, very high-contrast face: THE ONLY THIN THING ON THIS STREET, which is most of why it is here, because every other display face we hold is heavy -- a woodtype, a slab, a condensed grotesque, a fat rounded poster face. Frost on a thorn rather than a sign somebody painted.

literata.note: Sithen (§36), and everything that is not a heading. A serif drawn for reading on screens, set here without any atmosphere at all: the room is mostly a LIST OF RULES, and the argument is that rules like these are never written down plainly, so the one place they are written down plainly should look like it means it. One variable file serves both weights, as Chivo, Space Grotesk and Cinzel already do here.

petrona.note: Covenstead (§37), the headings and the h1. A workhorse text serif with a little roughness in it, set at display sizes ON PURPOSE: this room argues that the work is ordinary -- boots, tea, and going to the people nobody else goes to -- and a room about practical witchcraft that set itself in something gothic would be contradicting its own page in the typography.

asap.note: Covenstead (§37), everything that is not a heading. A plain, slightly rounded grotesque with no mystique whatsoever. One variable file serves both weights, as Chivo, Literata and Space Grotesk already do here.

bevan.note: Looming Rocks Amphitheatre (§38), the h1 and the marquee. A heavy slab with the weight of a board bolted to a rock face and repainted every few years. THE FOURTH HEAVY SLAB ON THIS STREET and told apart by era and by making: the campgrounds' Alfa Slab is ROUTED into wood by a machine, The Den's Ultra is a 1970s record sleeve, The Latibulum's Bree Serif is soft carpentry, and this is a painted venue sign.

archivo.note: Looming Rocks Amphitheatre (§38), everything that is not the marquee. A plain grotesque drawn for small sizes on screens, which is what a running order and a row of runtimes actually are. One variable file serves both weights, as Chivo, Literata and Space Grotesk already do here.

lexend.note: Dead Tired Society (§40), every word that is not the society's name or a heading. Lexend was drawn to reduce visual stress and ease reading fatigue, which is the one reason a room for the dead tired sets it: the face is doing some of the work so the reader does not have to. One variable file serves both weights, as Archivo, Chivo and Space Grotesk already do here.

sorts-mill-goudy.note: Dead Tired Society (§40), the society's name, its headings and nothing at reading size. A revival of Frederic Goudy's Oldstyle, which reads like a founding charter, and that is the joke: the grandest name on the street, set like an institution's, for a society whose members are lying on the floor.

bricolage-grotesque.note: Laughingstock (§41), every word that is read. Bricolage Grotesque is a grotesque drawn by Mathieu Triay out of the odd, slightly mismatched sans serifs of old French specimen books, and bricolage is making do with whatever is to hand -- which is most of what a disabled person's day is, and a good deal of what that room's comedy is about. It also sits in front of a brick wall. One variable file serves both weights, as Archivo, Chivo, Lexend and Space Grotesk already do here.

yellowtail.note: Laughingstock (§41), the neon over the stage and the club's name, and nothing at reading size. A 1950s sign-writer's script, which is the letterform a neon tube is bent into. A script carrying a sentence is an access failure wearing atmosphere -- the Doomscroll's blackletter rule -- so it never does.

limelight.note: The Lightbulb Picture House (§42), the picture house's name, its screen numbers and its headings, and nothing at reading size. An Art Deco display face of the kind cut into a 1930s picture house's fascia, which is where that room is set. It is not the Chappell's Monoton, which is a tube, or the Arcade's pixels: it is a carved sign over a door.

outfit.note: The Lightbulb Picture House (§42), every word that is read. A geometric sans with open, even letters and nothing fussy in them, because a relaxed screening is for people who have come to understand something, and the face should not be one more thing to get past. One variable file serves both weights, as Archivo, Chivo, Lexend and Space Grotesk already do here.

unbounded.note: Dance, Punks (§43), the room's name, its headings and the channel labels, and nothing at reading size. righteous.note: The Small Hours (§44), the diner's name, the sign on its roof, its headings and the dishes on the menu board, and nothing at reading size. The rounded, streamlined lettering bolted along the top of a mid-century roadside diner.

libre-franklin.note: The Small Hours (§44), every word that is read. A plain American gothic: the letter a menu board and a till receipt have always been set in. One variable file serves both weights.

patrick-hand.note: Nothing For Sale (§46), the name, the headings and the cardboard sign on each table: short labels and never a sentence. Neat capitals somebody writes on a sign propped against a table -- careful, one sign each, which is not Club Chronic's marker scrawled over a wall of paper.

figtree.note: Nothing For Sale (§46), every word that is read. A plain, friendly geometric sans. One variable file serves both weights.

fredoka.note: Samefood Cafe (§47), the cafe's name, its headings, the specials line and the names on the regulars' trays, and nothing at reading size. A round, fat, soft face whose every stroke ends in the same curve, like a plate that came out of one mould. One variable file serves both weights.

inclusive-sans.note: Samefood Cafe (§47), every word that is read. Olivia King drew it for legibility, with letters that cannot be taken for one another -- the room's rule that nothing on a plate is hidden in anything else, arriving at the level of the alphabet. hanken-grotesk.note: The Collection Collection (§48), every word that is read, on the labels and off them. One variable file serves both weights; no italic is shipped, and the room sets titles upright with font-synthesis off.

architects-daughter.note: The Map (§49), the lettering on every label, flag and sign on the model, and the page's name. albert-sans.note: The Map (§49), every sentence that is read, on the mat and off it. bagel-fat-one.note: Vital Plant Living (§50), the kitchen's name, its headings, the step names in the builder and the names on the board, and nothing at reading size. be-vietnam-pro.note: Vital Plant Living (§50), every word that is read: the pantry, the ticket, the notes on the board. An open, round-shouldered grotesque that is easy going down a long list, which is most of that page. Latin subset only, which is why the room does not claim the face's Vietnamese. Two weights, two files, no italic shipped.

varela-round.note: The Community Center (§51), the letterboard and nothing else: the room's name, the line over it and the headings, set in capitals the way push-in plastic letters sit in ribbed felt. radio-canada.note: The Community Center (§51), every word that is read: the house norms, the counter, the notes. dynapuff.note: The Dopamine Dress-Up Den (§52), the shop's name, its headings, the names of the rails and the looks, and nothing at reading size. plus-jakarta-sans.note: The Dopamine Dress-Up Den (§52), every word that is read: the rails, how each thing feels and how it comes off, the looks and the house rules. rammetto-one.note: Now Playing (§53), the title on the bill and the name of every room on it, and nothing at reading size. instrument-sans.note: Now Playing (§53), every word that is read: the line about each room, and the titles and running times read out of them. chango.note: Plural Mural (§54), every word painted on a mural and the room's name, and nothing at reading size. commissioner.note: Plural Mural (§54), every word that is read: what is on each mural, how the wall works and how to propose one. marcellus-sc.note: Community Library (§55), the lintel over the door, the room's name, every heading and the street door's name, and nothing at reading size. andika.note: Community Library (§55), every word that is read. gravitas-one.note: L-Space (§56), the room's name, every heading and the street-side door's words into it, and nothing at reading size. A very heavy, very high-contrast display face, and the name is the joke: in L-space enough weight bends everything near it. One weight, one static file.

libre-baskerville.note: Oook (§57), every word that is read, cream on the Librarian's rust. libre-caslon-text.note: Cavendish Coworking (§58), everything that is read: our words on the hall wall and the rooms' words on every note. Caslon's letter at reading size, in the Georgian house the room is built after. Static files, a real bold and a real italic.

atkinson-hyperlegible-next.note: The Broadsheet Broadside (§60), the sheet: every word on both sides of every broadside, the claim line at 800 and the heads at 700, and the room's own prose. bodoni-moda.note: The Broadsheet Broadside (§60), the ship's name painted along the hull and the room's headings, and NOTHING ON THE SHEET. leckerli-one.note: The Doom Scoop (§61), the room's name and the name on its street door, and nothing at reading size. A fat, soft brush script, the lettering painted on an ice cream parlour's window. A script carrying a headline would be an access failure wearing atmosphere, so it never does.

syne.note: Arlesglad Caverns (§62), the name of the caverns, its headings and the room names on the lift panel, and nothing at reading size. Wide, square-shouldered and a little pleased with itself, which is the glad in the name. Its figures are small old-style ones, so the level numbers are set in Rethink Sans. One variable file; the caverns set it at one weight only.

rethink-sans.note: Arlesglad Caverns (§62), every word that is read. A plain, open sans that stays readable in low light, because the only light down there is the handrail. One variable file serves both weights.

geologica.note: Stay Frosty (§63), every word in the room, heading and paragraph alike: a room of one temperature does not change its voice between the sign and the page. Full-height lining figures, which matters in a room built round a number. One variable file serves both weights.

comfortaa.note: Stay Breezy (§64), the room's name, its headings and the name on every fan, and nothing at reading size: round, open and even, with counters you could put your hand through, which is as near as a typeface gets to the shape of moving air. One weight.

urbanist.note: Stay Breezy (§64), every word that is read. A clear, even sans with open shapes, set on a pale wall under a room full of lamps. One variable file serves both weights.

caprasimo.note: Mycelium Munchies (§65), the restaurant's name, its headings and the name of every dish and every mushroom, and nothing at reading size: a soft, fat serif with round ends, the shape of a mushroom cap. One weight.

schibsted-grotesk.note: Mycelium Munchies (§65), every word that is read: the menu, what is in every dish, and the growing rooms. A plain, sturdy grotesque, the face of a kitchen's printed ticket rather than its sign. One variable file serves both weights.

red-hat-text.note: Big Steep Fermentables (§66), every word that is read, and every strength, which is the one number that has to be read before the pour. Clear, open figures. One variable file serves both weights.

poppins.note: Glow Go Gee Gaws (§67), every word that is read. A plain geometric sans; the toys are the loud part.

big-shoulders-stencil.note: Rebellion Rave Room (§68), the hangar's name, its headings, the bay number and every label on the rig, and nothing at reading size: a condensed stencil, which is how a hangar numbers its doors and how a flight case says what is in it. One weight.

exo-2.note: Rebellion Rave Room (§68), every word that is read: the warnings, the house rules, the channel list and every control. A squared, open sans that stays legible small and fast, which is what a warning sign has to be. One variable file serves both weights.

sour-gummy.note: The Cooldown Room (§69), the room's name, its headings and the name of every snack in the machine, and nothing at reading size: soft, round and a little chewy, the shape of a sweet. One weight.

kumbh-sans.note: The Cooldown Room (§69), every word that is read, and the machine's readout. A plain, soft-cornered sans with open counters, because a room for coming down from somewhere loud should be the easiest thing on the road to read. One variable file serves both weights.

jetbrains-mono.note: The MUD Room's command line: what you type and the words the Slake knows. Never a sentence you read.

old-standard-tt.note: The Events Room (§71), behind Cavendish Coworking's Events door: the watch room's headings, set like a nineteenth-century almanac. Never the light list.

holtwood-one-sc.note: The Campfire (§75), upstairs at Cavendish Coworking: the room's name and headings, a heavy wood type like letters burnt into a log. Never a sentence.

grandstander.note: The Fishbowl (§78), through a door off the Town Hall: the room's name and headings, round and bold like a bowl. Never a sentence.

ibm-plex-mono.note: Isha Snow's NeuroHome, imported from her own artifact: small labels, the map's lettering and the instrument plates. Her choice, not ours.

averia-serif-libre.note: Pando Calrissian (§84), the room's name and every heading, and nothing at reading size. Dan Sayers's Avería, the average of every font Google Web Fonts carried in November 2011, which is why it sets a room about one tree made of tens of thousands of stems. One weight, one static file.

averia-sans-libre.note: Pando Calrissian (§84), every word that is read: how the tree grows, what it keeps, the notes on the fence, the real one and the name. The sans of the same averaged superfamily as the headings. Static files, one per weight. No italic shipped, so the room sets nothing italic.
The bold of the above, a separate static file: the count, the buttons and every strong phrase.

noticia-text.note: The Fridge of Sighs (§85), every word in the room: the word on every magnet, the room's name set as magnets, and everything read round them. A sturdy news serif that holds up small, which is what a word on a magnet has to do. Static files, one per weight. No italic shipped, so the room sets nothing italic.
The bold of the above, a separate static file: the name's magnets, the headings and every strong phrase.

allerta-stencil.note: Count Me In (§86), the step numbers painted on the stairwell's walls, the room's name and every heading, and nothing at reading size. Matt McInerney's Allerta, drawn for signs read from a distance, in its stencil cut, because a stairwell's level numbers are sprayed through a stencil. One weight, one static file.

hind.note: Count Me In (§86), every word that is read: how the stair works, the lift, what it keeps. A plain sans with a real bold, which Allerta has not got. Static files, one per weight. No italic shipped, so the room sets nothing italic.
The bold of the above, a separate static file: the buttons and every strong phrase.

fuzzy-bubbles.note: Rescue A Cat (§87), the room's name, every heading and every cat's name, and nothing at reading size. Robert Leuschke's rounded letter with a soft, uneven edge, the nearest thing to fur a typeface has. One weight, one static file.

pt-sans.note: Rescue A Cat (§87), every word that is read: where the cat is, how rescuing works, what the shelter keeps. ParaType's public-type sans, drawn to be plain and read by anybody. Static files, one per weight. No italic shipped, so the room sets nothing italic.
The bold of the above, a separate static file: the buttons and every strong phrase.

paytone-one.note: Rescue A Dog (§88), the room's name, every heading and every dog's name, and nothing at reading size. Vernon Adams's heavy, round, friendly letter, which is how a dog comes at you across the snow. One weight, one static file.

open-sans.note: Rescue A Dog (§88), every word that is read. Steve Matteson's open, even sans. It ships as a variable font, so Google serves the same file for 400 and 700; it is downloaded once and declared twice against the weight axis, Radio Canada's call. No italic shipped.
Byte-identical to the 400 above; see that note.

carter-one.note: Rescue Small Animals (§89), the h1, every heading, each animal's name and the street door's name. A short, chunky, friendly display face, never a sentence.

balsamiq-sans.note: Rescue Small Animals (§89), every word that is read. A plain hand-drawn sans with open, distinct letters, like a label written on a carrier. No italic downloaded: the room sets none.
Its bold, a file of its own.

bellefair.note: The Brass Tacks Board (§90), the h1, every post's title and every heading: a high-contrast face cut like an engraved plate. Never a sentence.

merriweather.note: Its italic, a second alphabet, for a post's *emphasis*.

The Brass Tacks Board (§90), every word of every post and of the board around them. A serif drawn for reading on screens, sturdy enough to read off a brass plate.
